title: Leaf-Similar Trees
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<TreeNode*> s1: up to h1 entries (height of tree 1) → O(h)
- vector<TreeNode*> s2: up to h2 entries (height of tree 2) → O(h)
- not counted: input trees, returned bool
approach: Use an iterator-style DFS with an explicit stack for each tree. Each call to `nextLeaf` advances the DFS until it finds the next leaf, yielding one value at a time. Run both iterators in parallel, comparing leaves pairwise: return false on the first mismatch or when one tree exhausts before the other. This avoids collecting all leaves - only O(h) stack space is needed per tree, where h is tree height.
hints: What do you need to remember about tree 1's leaves while you are still discovering tree 2's leaves? Each tree has at most 200 nodes.

Use an iterator-style DFS with an explicit stack that yields one leaf at a time. For tree 1 in Example 1, the first `nextLeaf` call pops 3, pushes 1 then 5, pops 5, pushes 2 then 6, pops 6 → yields 6.

**Single node** - both trees are single leaves with the same value.
`Input: root1 = [1], root2 = [1]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: initializing the stack empty instead of pushing root → `nextLeaf` returns NONE immediately → returns false

**Different leaf counts** - one tree has more leaves than the other.
`Input: root1 = [1,2], root2 = [1,2,3]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning true when the first iterator exhausts without checking the second → returns true

**Same values, different order** - leaves have identical values but in different positions.
`Input: root1 = [1,2,3], root2 = [1,3,2]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: storing leaves in an unordered_set instead of comparing in sequence → returns true (both sets are {2, 3})

**Node with one child** - an internal node has only one child and must not be treated as a leaf.
`Input: root1 = [3,2,null,1], root2 = [1]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: using `!node->left || !node->right` instead of `!node->left && !node->right` for leaf check → treats one-child nodes as leaves → tree 1 yields [3, 2, 1] instead of [1] → returns false

followUps.q: What if each tree has up to 10^9 nodes and you receive them as a stream - can you still decide leaf-similarity?
followUps.a: The iterator approach already handles this. Each `nextLeaf` call only needs O(h) stack space and produces one leaf. You would implement `nextLeaf` as a stateful coroutine that pulls nodes from the stream on demand. TC: O(n), SC: O(h).

followUps.q: What if you need to check leaf-similarity for k trees simultaneously?
followUps.a: Run k iterators in parallel, comparing all k leaf values at each step. If any differ, return false. If all exhaust at the same step, return true. TC: O(n_total), SC: O(k · h_max).

followUps.q: Can you reduce the space to O(1) if you are allowed to temporarily modify the trees?
followUps.a: Use Morris traversal inside `nextLeaf` - temporarily redirect right pointers of nodes with left children to thread back to the successor, then restore them. Each call uses O(1) extra space beyond the tree itself. TC: O(n), SC: O(1).
